# ExactGround

> Free, open-source guard that stops AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) from installing npm or PyPI packages that do not exist (hallucinated packages / slopsquatting), versions that were never published, and young look-alikes of popular packages. Optional hosted MCP API checks that a function, class or method exists in an exact package version.

- Repository: https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground
- Website: https://alidaram99.github.io/exactground/
- Hosted API (MCP, pay per check): https://apify.com/dropin-apis/exactground-api — MCP endpoint https://dropin-apis--exactground-api.apify.actor/mcp (Authorization: Bearer <Apify token>)

## Quick answers

- Check names now: `npx -y github:alidaram99/exactground#v0.1.4 check pypi:reqeusts react@99.0.0`
- Claude Code: `claude plugin marketplace add alidaram99/exactground` then `claude plugin install exactground@exactground-marketplace` (PreToolUse hook on Bash|Write|Edit|MultiEdit).
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace add alidaram99/exactground --ref v0.1.4`, or `exactground init codex --write` (PreToolUse on Bash and apply_patch).
- Gemini CLI: `gemini extensions install https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground --ref v0.1.4` (BeforeTool hook), or `exactground init gemini --write`. Cursor: `exactground init cursor --write` (beforeShellExecution).
- Blocks: names missing from the registry, never-published pinned versions, npm security placeholders, look-alikes of top-3,000 packages that are < 180 days old or < 500 weekly downloads. Warns: new (< 30 days), low downloads, deprecated, yanked.
- Checks bare installs (`npm install`, `uv sync`, `poetry install`) against the lockfile, `pip install -r` files, and manifest edits/patches.
- Config: `.exactground.json` with `allow`, `privateScopes`, `strict`.
- Hosted tools: check_symbols ($0.002/symbol), check_packages ($0.0005/package), check_diff ($0.01/diff). npm types read with the TypeScript compiler (DefinitelyTyped fallback); Python wheels parsed statically, never executed. `exists: null` = not knowable statically.
- Evidence: A USENIX Security 2025 study (Spracklen et al.) had 16 models write 576,000 code samples; of the 2.23 million package recommendations in them, 440,445 (19.7%) named packages that do not exist (205,474 unique names). In a separate rerun of 500 prompts that had produced a hallucination, 10 times each, 43% of those hallucinated names came back in all 10 runs.
- Threat model: ExactGround stops an agent that hallucinates or mistypes a package name in a normal install command. It is a cooperative guardrail, not a sandbox against an agent deliberately evading it; use OS/container sandboxing for that.
- Out of scope: a same-user agent that deliberately obfuscates commands (program names or paths built at run time, own scripts, encoded commands) can defeat any hook-based guard, including ExactGround. This residual class is out of scope; for adversarial agents use an OS sandbox/container or a separate OS user. Details: https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground/blob/main/SECURITY.md
- Limits: agent hooks are guardrails, not a security boundary. Hooks deny on registry outage or internal error by default. Installs inside `node -e`/`python -c`, `$(...)` or `eval` are denied (cannot be checked). The cache never allows on the hook path. A project .exactground.json counts only after a human runs `exactground trust`.
- Hosted API status: live on the Apify Store since 2026-10-03 (https://apify.com/dropin-apis/exactground-api); calls need an Apify API token.
